== +/- easter things ==
{| class="wikitable"
!Offset from Easter
!Traditional Name (Western)
!Liturgical Significance
|-
|'''-5 Sundays'''
|'''Quinquagesima''' (or in modern Roman calendar, 8th Sunday in Ordinary Time if no pre-Lent)
|Last Sunday before Lent; prepares for Ash Wednesday.
|-
|'''-4 Sundays'''
|'''1st Sunday in Lent'''
|Beginning of Lent proper — fasting & penitence.
|-
|'''-3 Sundays'''
|'''2nd Sunday in Lent'''
|Focus on Transfiguration or other penitential readings.
|-
|'''-2 Sundays'''
|'''3rd Sunday in Lent'''
|Mid-Lent penitential themes.
|-
|'''-1 Sunday'''
|'''Palm Sunday'''
|Triumphal entry into Jerusalem; Passion reading.
|}
{| class="wikitable"
!Offset from Easter
!Traditional Name
!Liturgical Significance
|-
|'''0'''
|'''Easter Sunday'''
|Resurrection; high point of the liturgical year.
|-
|'''+1 Sunday'''
|'''Low Sunday''' (''Quasimodo Geniti'', Divine Mercy Sunday)
|Octave day of Easter; return to normal liturgy.
|-
|'''+2 Sundays'''
|'''Second after Easter''' (''Misericordia'')
|Good Shepherd Sunday in many traditions.
|-
|'''+3 Sundays'''
|'''Third after Easter'''
|Christ’s teachings before Ascension.
|-
|'''+4 Sundays'''
|'''Fourth after Easter'''
|Preparation for the Ascension.
|-
|'''+5 Sundays'''
|'''Fifth after Easter''' (''Rogation Sunday'' in traditional usage)
|Prayers for crops and blessings; processions before Ascension Thursday.
